 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Ajit Kumar
Oral Order
2 03-12-2025 Heard the parties.

2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Supaul PS Case No. 575 of 2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 74, 109, 115(2), 126(2), 303(2), 351(2)(3), 352 of the BNS,
2023 registered on 25.08.2024 by the informant, Nandan Yadav.

3. The prosecution story as per the informant, Nandan Yadav is that on 23/03/18 his wife Punisha Devi had purchased 5 kathas of land from the mother of the petitioner namely, Janki Devi and got jamabandi opened in his name.
It is further alleged that on 28/06/24 while the informant was irrigating his land, all the accused persons came there and started abusing and stopping him saying that the land belonged to them.
The informant told them that he had purchased the said land from their mother.

On this, all the accused persons after Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.78217 of 2025(2) dt.03-12-2025 being variously armed with lathi, sword, rod and country-made pistol came to the informant's darwaja and fired a gun shot.

Hearing the sound of gun shot when the informant and his wife came out of their house, then the accused, namely, Ruban Yadav ordered the accused/petitioner, Anil Yadav to kill them, upon which the petitioner, Anil Yadav, with intention to kill, gave sword blow on his head causing bleeding injury on the right front side of his head.
He fell down on the ground, then all the accused persons started indiscriminately beating him by lathi- danda.
When informant's wife came to his rescue, she was also abused and assaulted by the accused persons.

Lastly, on the intervention of the villagers, the informant and his wife were rescued and Anil Yadav @ Anil Kumar Yadav vs The State Of Bihar on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81102818/
1 taken to the Hospital, Supaul.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the FIR.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioner has falsely been implicated in this case on the ground of land dispute between the parties and the injuries which are said to have been sustained by the informant do not corroborate the allegations levelled against this petitioner in the FIR.

It has next been submitted that despite allegations having been levelled against this petitioner to have caused injury with sword, the nature of injury sustained does not corroborate the same Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.78217 of 2025(2) dt.03-12-2025 while there are altogether three accused persons in this case, out of which two persons have already been extended the privilege of anticipatory bail by the learned trial court itself and this petitioner though has got four criminal antecedents out of which one case is related to Section 498A of the IPC and other two are of Excise Act and one though is akin to the present one but he is on bail in all the four cases.
It has next been submitted that there is an unexplained delay of twelve days in filing of the FIR and the incident is said to have taken place for existing land dispute between the parties.

5. Learned APP vehemently opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner submitting that the petitioner seems to be habitual offender as he has got four criminal antecedent under his belt,
therefore, he does not deserve the privilege of anticipatory bail.

6. Considering the existing land dispute between the parties, the injuries which are said to have been sustained by the informant do not corroborate the allegations levelled against this petitioner in the FIR, this Court is inclined to extend the petitioner the privilege of anticipatory bail.
7. Let the petitioner be released on bail, in the event of their arrest or surrender before the subordinate court within a Patna High Court CR.

(iv) the petitioners shall in no way try to induce or promise or threat the witnesses or tamper with the evidences, failing which the State shall be at liberty to take steps for cancellation of the bail bonds.
